<section begin=par86/>arising from ''ăy'', in {{GHGheb|text=אִשֶּׁה|translate=belonging to fire}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֵשׁ}}), i.e. a ''sacrifice offered by fire''; {{GHGheb|text=לִבְנֶה}} (prop. ''milky'') ''the storax-shrub'', Arabic ''lubnay''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|k}}
6. ''Abstract'' nouns formed from ''concretes'' by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=וּת}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}[{{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}] ({{GHGpar|95|t}}), cf. our terminations ''-dom, -hood, -ness'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַלְדוּת|translate=youth}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכוּת|translate=kingdom}} (the omission of the {{GHGterm|Dageš}} in {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}} shows that the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} is weakened from a full vowel; on ''malik'' as underlying the present form {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}} cf. {{GHGpar|84|a|a}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמָנוּת|translate=widowhood}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמָן|translate=widower}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמָנָה|translate=widow}}. In Aram. this fem. ending {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} (or {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} with rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}}) is a common termination of the infinitive in the derived conjugations (cf., as substantival infinitives of this kind, {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמָעוּת|translate=the announcing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}}, and {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַבְּרוּת|translate=the making of a league}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=23}}); in Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} as a termination to express abstract ideas (including some which appear to be directly derived from the verbal stem, as {{GHGheb|text=סִכְלוּת|translate=folly}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִפְאוּת|translate=a heating}}<ref>[See a complete list of instances in König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, ii. 1, p. 205 f.]</ref>) becomes more common only in the later books. It is affixed to adjectives ending in ''î'' (see above, h) in {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזְרִיּוּת|translate=cruelty}}, and {{GHGheb|text=קֽוֹמְמִיּוּת|translate=upright position}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=13}}, used adverbially).

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|l}}
The ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}} is found earlier, e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵרִית|translate=remainder}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֵאשִׁית|translate=principium}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רֵאשׁ}}={{GHGheb|text=רֹאשׁ}} (''head'') ''princeps''. The termination ''ôth'' seems to occur in {{GHGheb|text=הָכְמוֹת|translate=wisdom}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, joined to a ''singular''; so also {{GHGheb|text=חַכְמוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=1}}, where, probably, {{GHGheb|text=חָכְמוֹת}} should likewise be read) and in {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹלֵלוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=17}}, &c., with the parallel form {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹלֵלוּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=13}}.
<section end=par86/>
<section begin=par87/>{{GHGpar-heading|87|Of the Plural}}

<div style="font-size: small; text-align: center;">Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 426 ff., and on the feminines, p. 441 ff.; M. Lambert, ‘Remarques sur la formation du pluriel hébreu,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxiv. 99 ff., and ‘Les anomalies du pluriel des noms en Hébreu,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xliii. 206 ff.; P. ''Lajčiak'', ''Die Plural- u. Dualendungen im semit. Nomen'', Lpz. 1903; J. Barth, ‘Beiträge zur Pluralbildung des Semit.,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1904, p. 431 ff., i. ‘the ''ai'' of the constr. st.’</div>

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|a}}
'''1.''' The regular ''plural'' termination for the ''masculine gender'' is {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, always with the tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סוּס|translate=horse}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=סוּסִים|translate=horses}}; but also very often written defectively {{GHGheb|text=־ִם}}, especially when in the same word one of the vowel letters, {{GHGheb|text=ו}} or {{GHGheb|text=י}}, precedes, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּנִּינִם}}. Nouns in {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} make their plural in {{GHGheb|text=־ִיִּים}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִי|translate=a Hebrew}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְריִּים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=18}}); but usually contraction takes place, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים|translate=crimson garments}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|b}}
Nouns in {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} lose this termination when they take the plural ending, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֹזֶה|translate=seer}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=חֹזִים}} (cf. {{GHGpar|75|h}}).—In regard to the loss of the tone from the {{GHGheb|text=־ִם}} in the two old plurals {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם|translate=water}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַ֫יִם|translate=heaven}}, cf. {{GHGpar|88|d}} and § 96.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|c}}
The termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} is sometimes assumed also by feminines (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נָשִׁים|translate=women}}, § 96 under {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים|translate=years}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}}; {{GHGheb|text=רְחֵלִים|translate=ewes}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רָחֵל}}), so that an indication of gender is not necessarily implied in it (cf. also below, m–p).—On the use of this termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} to express abstract, extensive, and intensive ideas, cf. {{GHGpar|124}}.
